items.text: POPULATION, MIGRATION AND DISASTERS
Class 8 Geography | Sample notes
MIGRATION – Movement of people
Migration is the movement of people from one place to another.
Push factors: lack of jobs, poverty and droughts in villages.
Pull factors: better jobs, schools and hospitals in cities.
Effects: crowded cities and the growth of slums.
Movement from villages to cities is called rural-urban migration.
URBANISATION – Growth of towns and cities
bold: URBANISATION – Growth of towns and cities

items.text: Urbanisation is the growth in the share of people living in towns and cities.
items.topic: URBANISATION – Growth of towns and cities

items.text: Causes: industries and better jobs in cities.
items.topic: URBANISATION – Growth of towns and cities

items.text: Effects: traffic jams, pollution and a shortage of housing.
items.topic: URBANISATION – Growth of towns and cities

items.text: Measures: planned cities and better public transport.
items.topic: URBANISATION – Growth of towns and cities

items.text: EARTHQUAKES – Sudden shaking of the ground
bold: EARTHQUAKES – Sudden shaking of the ground

items.text: An earthquake is a sudden shaking of the ground.
items.topic: EARTHQUAKES – Sudden shaking of the ground

items.text: Causes: movement of the tectonic plates under the Earth's surface.
items.topic: EARTHQUAKES – Sudden shaking of the ground

items.text: The point on the surface right above where it starts is the epicentre.
items.topic: EARTHQUAKES – Sudden shaking of the ground

items.text: It is measured on the Richter scale.
items.topic: EARTHQUAKES – Sudden shaking of the ground

items.text: Effects: collapse of buildings and loss of life.
items.topic: EARTHQUAKES – Sudden shaking of the ground

items.text: Precautions: take cover under a strong table and stay away from windows.
items.topic: EARTHQUAKES – Sudden shaking of the ground

items.text: QUICK COMPARISON
Migration = people move (pushed out, pulled in)
Urbanisation = cities grow (jobs in, traffic out)
Earthquakes = the ground shakes (plates move)
